--- title: "Your data and its processing (page 1)" --- ::: {.cell} ::: Page 1 of the app, **Input data and processing**, is where everything starts: you describe the project, upload the MS-DIAL file, read it and process it. This chapter shows how the file must be structured, what QuaNTA checks when it reads it, and what the processing settings do. ## The data file QuaNTA reads the **alignment result** exported from [MS-DIAL](https://systemsomicslab.github.io/compms/msdial/main.html) (*Export → Alignment result*, peak areas) as a tab-delimited `.txt` file. Upload it as it is, or compressed as `.zip` or `.gz` with that one file inside. The file has two parts: four rows of **sample information** at the top, and below them one row per **feature** (a compound or an unknown peak) with its peak area in every sample. This is the top-left corner of the example file: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Class Blk C0 C0-005 C0-01
File type Blank Standard Standard Standard
Injection order 1 2 3 4
Batch ID 1 1 1 1
Alignment ID Average Rt(min) Average Mz Metabolite name Comment MS/MS spectrum PROCBLK3_B1_1 Cal0_E_B1_2 Cal0-005_E_B1_3 Cal0-01_E_B1_4
16572 13.016 219.17401 (+)-Nootkatone Quant 2698760 0 419457 749115
5569 9.437 136.02139 1,3-benzothiazole Quant 2713850 131522 0 0
19717 8.393 240.14929 1,3-Di-o-tolylguanidine Quant 1685925 0 0 384821
15351 7.449 212.11803 1,3-Diphenylguanidine Quant 100897380 1928345 2064414 2317076
````` ::: ::: **The four sample rows** (shaded) describe each sample column: | Row | Content | In QuaNTA | |---|---|---| | `Class` | the group of the sample, e.g. `Healthy`, `QC1`, `C0-5` | the groups in figures and statistics | | `File type` | `Sample`, `QC`, `Standard` or `Blank` | study sample, QC, calibration sample or (method) blank | | `Injection order` | a number | the order along the run (drift, figures over the sequence) | | `Batch ID` | a number | blank subtraction and calibration per batch | **The feature columns** QuaNTA needs (exact names): `Alignment ID`, `Average Rt(min)`, `Average Mz`, `Metabolite name` and `Comment`. Other columns are ignored. ### Naming conventions The **`Comment`** column tells QuaNTA what each feature is: | Comment | Meaning | |---|---| | `Quant` | a targeted compound, quantified with a calibration curve | | `Quant\` | a targeted compound with a compound class after the backslash, e.g. `Quant\ATZ` | | `IS` | an isotope-labelled internal standard | | `IS\` | an internal standard with a compound class, e.g. `IS\ATZ` | | `vIS` | the volumetric internal standard (added to check and correct the volume) | | `R` | removed from the data when it is read | | empty or anything else | a non-targeted feature | The **calibration samples** (`File type` = `Standard`) carry their concentration in the sample name, after `Cal`, with a dash for the decimal point: `Cal0` (the zero calibrant), `Cal0-005` (0.005), `Cal0-5` (0.5), `Cal10` (10). **QC samples** with the same `Class` are replicates of one QC material; several QC materials (e.g. `QC-low`, `QC-high`) are possible. The example file has 196 targeted compounds, 22 internal standards, 1 volumetric internal standard and 1000 non-targeted features, measured in 299 samples in 3 batches. ::: {.callout-warning} ## Check before uploading When you click **Process data**, QuaNTA lists `Comment` values that do not follow the conventions (e.g. `quant`, `IS-ATZ`) and column names that look like the required ones but are not exact (e.g. `Comment2`). Values that look like `Quant` or `IS` are shown in red: they would be treated as non-targeted. Fix them in MS-DIAL or in the file and upload again. ::: ## Uploading and reading 1. Fill in the **project information** (title, user, unit of the concentrations). It goes into the reports. 2. Optionally **load a parameters file** (`.yml`) saved earlier with *Download settings*; the example has `example_data/QuaNTA_example_parameters.yml`. Loading one replaces all settings and removes the results of a previous run (QuaNTA asks first). 3. **Upload the data file** and click **Read data file**. The *Data reading log* on the right shows what was read; page 2 then shows an overview of the data. ## Processing settings The settings are grouped as in the app. Hover the ⓘ next to each in the app for the full explanation; options that the data cannot support (e.g. a volumetric IS option without a vIS) are greyed out. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Click **Process data** to run all steps. Before it starts, a popup lists anything worth checking: settings that were corrected (e.g. a number outside its range), `Comment` values and column names that do not follow the conventions, and notes on the data (e.g. no targeted compounds, or batches that will use the global calibration curve). The *Processing log* shows the progress; when it is done, pages 3 and 4 show the results. ::: {.callout-tip} ## Save your settings **Download settings (.yml)** saves the project information and all settings, with the name of the dataset. Load the file later to process the same way, or use it with the command-line version (`run_quanta.R`). :::
